candidate_global_language.name: FIXED_POINT_PLUS_UNIFORM_FINITE_RING_SOLVABILITY_OPERATORS
candidate_global_language.scope: A candidate implicit global language extending fixed-point reasoning with exact operators that decide solvability of definable linear equation systems over finite rings/commutative rings, including prime-power cyclic-ring phenomena such as Z_{p^e}.

source.title: Definability of linear equation systems over groups and rings

facts_used: The finite group/ring linear-system solvability problems studied are polynomial-time decidable.
Solvability over Abelian groups and arbitrary finite rings can be logically reduced to solvability over commutative rings in the framework developed by the authors.
The work provides closure/normal-form results for logics extended with solvability operators.
These solvability problems are not expressible in plain FPC, so ring-solvability operators provide genuine additional exact algebraic capability.

relation_to_previous_barriers.R44AH: Original fixed-prime rank logic misses uniform field-parametrized rank.
relation_to_previous_barriers.R44AI: Even all finite-field linear-algebraic operators do not capture PTIME; ring-valued CFI phenomena expose a boundary beyond fields.
relation_to_previous_barriers.R44AJ: Moves exactly into that ring-solvability direction, but does not invent a universal theorem where the audited literature does not supply one.

literature_audit_result.searched_question: Does fixed-point logic augmented with sufficiently uniform finite-ring/module solvability operators provably capture PTIME, or is there a published theorem showing that this precise all-ring solvability extension still fails to capture PTIME?
literature_audit_result.important_note: Failure to locate a theorem is not proof that no theorem exists. This artifact records the audited frontier only and must be updated if stronger literature is found.

Legend_effect.L2: NOT_REFUTED; exact ring-solvability subroutines can be sound within their proved scope

next_rule.statement: Do not escalate to a more exotic algebraic domain merely by analogy. Either find a theorem deciding this ring-solvability language frontier, or leave the descriptive-logic ladder and return to a directly specified 3CNF transition law whose total polynomial work can be proved/refuted without relying on language-capture speculation.
